title: Record the review of phase 2: two findings, both fixed
message: Record the review of phase 2: two findings, both fixed

title: Name both pet tests that migrate the permanent tables in the testing guide
message:
Name both pet tests that migrate the permanent tables in the testing guide

The guide named Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans
as the one pet test that touches the permanent pet tables, and said the
booted suite applies migration 2026091007 on every fresh database. Since
b06a2367f Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent runs
the migrations on those tables too, and with the boot skipped one of the
two tests is what applies 2026091007.

Two suites started together on a database that has not been migrated both
run the migrations, and one fails on a version the other just recorded.
The guide says so.

Review of MR !24, finding 2. Work item #18.

title: Keep the pet legacy-migration test's write off the permanent pet_data
message:
Keep the pet legacy-migration test's write off the permanent pet_data

Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent sets owner_id
on every pet_data row to check the migrated column's range. The statement
is written for the fixture's temporary table. When the fixture is not in
place the name is the permanent table, and since b06a2367f that happens
whenever the migration run on the permanent tables fails: a key added by
hand, a user without CREATE, two suites started together on a database
that has not been migrated. Every saved pet then carried an owner_id no
owner has.

The statement now runs only when the fixture was created. It is the one
write below that point; the rest are reads, and the second migration run
already waits for the first.

Review of MR !24, finding 1. Work item #18.

title: Give the pet legacy-migration test the permanent tables it reads
message:
Give the pet legacy-migration test the permanent tables it reads

Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent failed on a
database built from sql/master_schema.sql alone. Its fixture hides
pet_data, pet_save_objs and schema_migrations behind temporary tables and
records migration 2026091007 as applied, because InnoDB refuses a foreign
key on a temporary table. verify_pet_persistence_schema() reads the key
from information_schema, which lists the permanent tables only, so the
test passed only where a boot or the live-schema test had already put the
key on the permanent pet_save_objs.

The test now runs the pet migrations on the permanent tables before it
creates the temporary ones. The migrations and master_schema.sql are
unchanged: started from the master_schema.sql shape they add the key, as
Test_pet_live_schema_cascades_objects_and_rejects_orphans checks.

Work item #18.
